title: Bishop's letter emphasizes importance of prayer in maintaining focus on God
text:
Bishop’s letter emphasizes importance of prayer in maintaining focus on God
Bishop James Noonan addressed the community in a letter published on Aug. 19, emphasizing the essential role of prayer in keeping focus on God and guiding the faithful along a righteous path.
In his message, Noonan reflected on St. Paul's teachings about God's divine attributes—riches, wisdom, and knowledge—and described them as challenging for people to comprehend from an earthly perspective. He wrote, "As God created the sky and the earth and all within it, so we are. His majesty comes not from the secular idea of royalty, but the majesty of Divine Love. This is His offering to each one of us, all our days." Noonan continued by highlighting that prayer is central to maintaining this relationship with God: "Prayer is essential to keep our focus on God, to guide our right path, and to transfigure our activity as a community of faith into the face of Jesus."
Noonan cited historical Church figures such as Pope Leo XIV and Pope St. Paul VI to reinforce his points about communal worship and liturgical life. He quoted Pope St. Paul VI: "God comes first; prayer is our primary duty; the liturgy is the primary source of the divine life communicated to us, the primary school of our spiritual life." The bishop also discussed how practices like celebrating Eucharist and praying Liturgy of the Hours serve as vital expressions of faith throughout daily life.
He addressed challenges faced by believers both past and present regarding distractions from prayer: "There were distractions while Jesus lived, just as there are distractions today to keep us from prayer... If we do not place ourselves in the presence of God, we will move away from God." The letter included words from St. John Vianney: "This is the glorious duty of man: to pray and to love... Prayer is nothing else but union with God ... God and the soul are fused together like two bits of wax that no one can ever pull apart.”
The Diocese of Orlando was established in 1968 and encompasses Brevard, Lake, Marion, Orange, Osceola, Polk, Seminole, Sumter, and Volusia Counties; it includes 79 parishes along with missions and Catholic schools under Bishop Noonan's leadership, according to The Diocese of Orlando.
Noonan concluded his letter by encouraging continued commitment through prayer: “Through our prayer may we come to understand the depth of riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!”
